subject: POC operational commitments & KPI manifest
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@orionanalytics.com>, Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@orionanalytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Sep 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: POC operational commitments & KPI manifest

Hi Samir / Alex —

Thanks again for the call today. Per our discussion, I wanted to get a concise operational checklist and readout of success criteria so we can lock the POC timeline. Attached is a first-pass matrix (orion_poc_matrix.xlsx) — the two asks: 1) confirm the evaluation dataset owners and golden-test prompts, 2) sign off on the three gating KPIs below so we can provision Dedicated capacity and start baseline runs next week.

Proposed high-level success criteria (please confirm):
- Latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms for interactive prompts (95th measured under steady-state test traffic).
- Throughput: 30 sustained requests/sec across the endpoint (burst to 90 req/sec acceptable for daytime peaks).
- Cost: average cost/token < $0.0009 (target to hit budget envelope for production estimates).
- Quality: top-line intent-match > 92% on golden set; hallucination rate < 2% on closed-domain fact checks.

Operational commitments / owners: 
- Redwood: baseline performance run + telemetry dashboard (Marcus)
- Orion: provide 3 canonical prompt sets + labeled expected outputs (Alex)
- Shared: nightly ingestion job for test corpus and weekly sync (Neha / Alex)

Timeline (proposed):
- 2026-09-07: Orion provides test prompts and labels (poe_test_prompts.csv)
- 2026-09-10: Redwood completes baseline run (no optimizations) and shares baseline metrics
- 2026-09-14 to 09-28: Iterative tuning window (quantization/ batching/ cache rules), daily traces
- 2026-09-30: POC readout and go/no-go decision

Next steps: confirm owners and acceptance targets; if you agree we will push Dedicated capacity reservation tomorrow to meet the baseline run date.

Thanks,

Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0122

Attachment: orion_poc_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)
Attachment: poe_test_prompts.csv (CSV, 3k rows)

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@orionanalytics.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@orionanalytics.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 08 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: POC operational commitments & KPI manifest

Lauren —

Thanks, this is helpful. Confirming Orion can deliver the labeled golden prompts by 09-07 (we'll push to 09-06 EOD) and we will also include a short set of adversarial examples to test hallucination. A few clarifications from our side: 

- For latency we care most about p95 under 95th-percentile concurrent users — your proposed p95 < 350ms is OK but can we add a separate tail requirement for long-context prompts (20–30k tokens)? For long-context items, target p95 < 900ms.
- Throughput: 30 req/sec sustained is fine; we will validate at 45 req/sec in the mid-test to simulate peak load.
- Cost/token: target of <$0.0009 is acceptable for the POC budget.
- Quality: we can provide the golden set metrics; we want a minimum of 90% intent-match and hallucination < 3% for the initial pass.

One ask: please include a short acceptance matrix in the baseline readout that lists pass/fail per KPI and owner sign-off checkbox. Also add a column for fallback policy if a KPI fails (eg route to smaller model or throttle).

Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Integrations, Orion Analytics
samir.patel@orionanalytics.com
+1 (206) 555-4491

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@orionanalytics.com>, Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@orionanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Sep 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: POC operational commitments & KPI manifest

Lauren / team —

I reviewed Samir's note and updated the attached trial statement (redwood_trial_statement.pdf) to include: long-context tail SLA (p95 < 900ms), a throughput validation stage at 45 req/sec, and an acceptance matrix with explicit owner columns and fallback policies. Highlights from my baseline plan: 

- Baseline run (09-10): standard model, no quantization; capture p50/p95/p99, throughput, token-cost calc, and qualitative sample outputs.
- Optimization pass (09-14 to 09-25): try 4/8-bit quantization profiles, dynamic batching windows, and KV-cache heuristics.
- Quality checks: compute intent-match and hallucination rate across golden/test sets; assign thresholds as Samir suggested (>=90% intent-match to pass initial).

I've put Marcus on the dashboard setup and request a short Slack channel with Orion to circulate traces and flame graphs during the tuning window. If we see a quality regression after quantization we'll fall back to a higher-precision variant and note the impact on cost/token in the acceptance matrix.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_trial_statement.pdf (PDF, 4 pages)
